project.name: KirokuForge
project.goal: Provide reliable provenance-backed project memory for agents and users.

records.title: Canonical JSON memory
records.summary: memory.json is the only editable source of truth.

payload.decision: Use kiroku/memory.json as the canonical project-memory artifact.
payload.context: Agents and user-facing projections need one authoritative representation.
implications: Generated Markdown and bootstrap files are projections.
Canonical mutations must validate against the memory schema.

records.title: Linear supersession history
records.summary: Historical replacement uses one predecessor and one direct successor without cycles.

payload.decision: Preserve replaced knowledge through atomic linear supersession chains.
payload.context: Historical claims must remain inspectable without allowing ambiguous replacement graphs.
implications: A superseded record has exactly one direct replacement.
A replacement supersedes exactly one direct predecessor.
Branches, merges, cycles, and later edits to historical predecessors are rejected.

records.title: Maintain KirokuForge development memory
records.summary: The project-local kiroku directory is the official durable memory for development of the skill itself.

payload.decision: Maintain kiroku/ in this project as the official development memory for KirokuForge.
payload.context: The skill is developed using its own memory model so decisions, milestones, evidence, and rationale remain reusable across sessions.
implications: Update canonical memory at the end of meaningful development sessions.
Regenerate projections from memory.json after each update.
This dogfooding choice does not prescribe where other users store their memories.

records.title: Provenance-backed durable claims
records.summary: Durable memory distinguishes observed evidence from inference.

payload.decision: Attach structured source evidence to durable claims and preserve explicit uncertainty.
payload.context: Future agents must understand both what is believed and why.
implications: Verified claims require direct supporting evidence.
Sources use stable locators, revisions, and hashes when available.

records.title: Version-control independent operation
records.summary: KirokuForge treats source revisions as opaque identifiers and does not invoke version-control tools.

payload.decision: Keep KirokuForge independent from Git and all other version-control systems.
payload.context: Memory storage and source verification must work for local, external, or independently managed artifacts.
implications: Revision values are opaque identifiers supplied by the user or agent.
The CLI validates captured hashes and internal consistency without resolving external revisions.
Versioning, backup, and synchronization remain outside the skill boundary.

records.title: Generated projections are read-only
records.summary: Markdown views and the agent bootstrap must be regenerated from canonical JSON.

payload.constraint: Do not edit generated Markdown views or agent-bootstrap.json as source data.
consequences: Regenerate projections with render, bootstrap, or build.
Discard projection-only changes that are not represented in memory.json.

relations.note: Read-only projections preserve a single source of truth.

records.title: Single active mutation run
records.summary: Only one run may be active and build waits for its completion.

payload.constraint: A memory may contain at most one running run, and projections must not be built until it is completed.
consequences: Published projections cannot represent a partially completed operation.

records.title: P0 controlled writes complete
records.summary: The controlled write core is implemented and verified at commit e598905.

payload.statement: At commit e598905, KirokuForge implements controlled sources, run lifecycle, record creation, optimistic updates, atomic supersession, validation, rendering, and bootstrap generation; 62 tests pass.

records.title: Controlled memory mutation pipeline
records.summary: The CLI manages source registration, runs, record lifecycle, validation, and projection builds.

payload.detail: Canonical writes flow through add-source, start-run, add-record or update-record or supersede-record, finish-run, and build.

records.title: Incremental source hash status
records.summary: source-status identifies unchanged, changed, and new local inputs before an update run.

payload.detail: source-status compares local file SHA-256 values with the latest source registered for each URI, returns deterministic JSON, and never mutates canonical memory.
components: latest captured source selection per URI

records.title: Optimistic record updates
records.summary: Record replacement requires the current content hash and preserves stable identity.

payload.detail: update-record performs complete semantic replacement only when --expect-hash matches, preserving id, key, type, and created_at while refreshing updated_at, generated_by, and content_hash.

records.title: Dedicated user memory UI
records.summary: The user proposed a dedicated interface over the structured memory store.

payload.description: Keep structured canonical files optimized for agents and build a dedicated UI for users to inspect and interact with project memory.
payload.expected_value: Improve navigation and comprehension without making Markdown a competing source of truth.

records.title: Add selective agent queries
records.summary: The query command is implemented with filters for key, type, status, scope, tag, relation-target, and relation-type, with sorting and multiple output formats.

payload.outcome: The query command supports filtering by key, type, status, scope, tag, relation-target, and relation-type, combined as a single relation when both target and type are specified. Enum validation rejects unknown values. Output formats: compact, full, ids. Sorting by title, type, status, created_at, updated_at (datetime). --count flag.

records.title: Complete P1 agent efficiency
records.summary: Selective queries, compact bootstrap output, and incremental source checks are implemented and verified.

payload.outcome: P1 provides compact agent context, selective record queries, and read-only incremental source detection through content hashes, without depending on external version-control systems.
